value: In FTD, increasing Reserve Index was associated with reduced connectivity in the Executive Network in the left middle frontal gyrus. These findings suggest that higher cognitive reserve is associated with greater network disconnection for a comparable degree of dementia severity.

spans.text: We might therefore speculate that, in our cohort of patients, those individuals with higher cognitive reserve need more disconnecting damage within the networks more remarkably targeted in FTD pathology to exhibit similar cognitive disability, as compared to those with lower cognitive reserve.

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were preprocessed with SPM8: the first four volumes were discarded for T1 equilibration; head motion was corrected, slice-timing differences were compensated, images were normalized to the SPM8 EPI template in Montreal Neurological Institute coordinates, smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM 3D Gaussian kernel, and filtered at 0.01–0.08 Hz. Group ICA was then performed with GIFT to identify network components and generate subject-specific Z-score maps.
